To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stability of carbon stocks in deep soil layers depends on the availability of fresh organic carbon.
the stability of organic matter in deep soil layers can be maintained in the absence of new plant derived carbon, but can be broken by the supply of new carbon.

the supply of plant-derived organic carbon to deep soil layers stimulates microbial mineralization of ancient carbon and that this process may control the stability of organic soil carbon stocks in deep soil layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a key question in soil science: how is soil carbon stored and how does it change over time?

understanding how the carbon cycle is controlled and regulated by soil microbes and how this knowledge can be used to predict the impact of climate change on soil organic carbon stocks in agricultural soils.
the stability of the world's soil carbon pool.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability of organic soil carbon in deep layers is controlled by fresh carbon input.
the stability of organic matter in deep soil layers depends on the availability of fresh plant derived organic matter.
the stability of soil carbon stocks is controlled by the availability of fresh carbon and that this availability is a function of land use and agricultural management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of soil carbon is determined by the balance between the supply of fresh carbon and the microbial activity.
the stability of organic C in deep soil layers can be maintained for millennia in the absence of new fresh C input.
the supply of organic matter to deep soil layers is essential for the stability of the soil carbon stock.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of organic matter is not just a function of its physical protection, as previously thought.
soil organic matter is not stable and that the stability of soil carbon is not a function of depth.
the stability of organic matter in the subsoil is controlled by the supply of fresh carbon.
